description: The phonemic gaps of the Linear A syllabary against the Proto-Semitic consonants: the signs whose values fill them, the gaps written by neutralization or left open, and the positional behaviour of the frequent unknown signs. A sign value's standing and confidence are those of sign_values.json.

methodology.gap_identification: Compare the standard Linear A CV grid (55 signs: 5 vowels + 12 consonant series × ~5 vowels) against the phonemic inventories of Northwest Semitic (Ugaritic/Canaanite), Luwian, and Middle Egyptian—the three language families attested in the Bronze Age Cretan administrative corpus.
methodology.candidate_selection: Unknown signs are candidates only if they show syllabic positional behavior (appearing word-initially, medially, and finally). Signs that appear predominantly standalone or with quantities are likely ideograms/logograms and are excluded.
methodology.standing: Each sign value carries its standing in sign_values.json: resolved (support independent of a Semitic match), proposed, or speculative (held in the sign's record only), with its confidence there.

vowels.note: No phonemic /e/ or /o/ in PS; these develop later via vowel shifts (Canaanite ā > ō, a > e near gutturals)

proto_semitic_inventory.linear_a_coverage: The standard 55-sign CV grid covers 12 consonant series. PS 29 consonants must map onto these 12 via neutralization (voicing, emphasis, place). The proposed values (*314=ḤA, *118=ṬA, *306=ʿA, *21F=HA, PA₃=BA, ZU=ṮU, *305=ḎA) extend coverage to ~19 consonant series, still short of the full 29.

cuneiform_parallels.description: Cuneiform scribes faced the identical phoneme-to-sign mapping problem. Their solutions parallel Linear A strategies.

sibilant_encoding.rule: Palaeosyrian/Old Akkadian used three sign series for sibilants + interdentals: ŠA/ŠI/ŠU for interdental ṯ; SA/SI/SU for sibilants š/ś; ZA/ZI/ZU for voiced interdentals ḏ/ẓ
sibilant_encoding.linear_a_parallel: Linear A uses SA/SI/SU for all sibilants (š/ś/s/ṣ merged) and ZA/ZE + ZU for interdentals/affricates. Same compression, same ambiguity.

velar_neutralization.rule: Cuneiform never distinguishes final k/g/q. Initial distinction partial: GAB = gab/qab, AG = ag/ak/aq. K-class neutralization is standard, not a flaw.
velar_neutralization.linear_a_parallel: Linear A KA/KI/KU neutralizes k/g/q identically. QA/QE/QI partially extends the grid for emphatic uvular. *34=QI completion mirrors cuneiform attempts to distinguish q.

pharyngal_marking.rule: Old Assyrian still marked pharyngal ḥ with dedicated signs (ḥapārum 'to dig'). Later Akkadian lost all guttural distinctions.
pharyngal_marking.linear_a_parallel: Linear A *314=ḤA preserves pharyngal marking—a scribal strategy parallel to Old Assyrian, and more conservative than standard Akkadian practice.

Q.neutralizes: partially covers uvular /q/; *34 = QI is proposed (0.70), with ai (Linear B a₅) another possible value

J.note: *28B = JI and JU = /lu/ (liquid; yu another possible value) are proposed; JA and JE are standard.

extra_signs.PA3: pa₃ = /ba/ (proposed, 0.90: voiced bilabial stop, see filled_gaps)
extra_signs.TA2: ta₂ (Linear B *66; resolved, /ta/ 0.65; a marked dental, written apart from TA on PK1. See the interdentals gap)
extra_signs.ZO: zo (AB20, 2 occurrences): both standalone with numerals (KH57, THEZg5), logographic in commodity lists. It would fill a Z-series /zo/ if syllabographic, but no syllabic word context tests it.
extra_signs.NWA: nwa (AB48, 1 occurrence): a hapax in JA-I-NWA-RO (SYZa4, Syme libation table; RILA-S1 p. 84 prints NWA), a complex onset /nw-/ outside the CV grid. JA-I-NWA-RO is read yā ʾanwaru 'O Radiant One' (vocative + elative of √n-w-r), SPECULATIVE 0.3.

filled_gaps.neutralization: Pharyngeal ḥ (Semitic) and velar ḫ (Luwian, Egyptian) neutralized into one sign

key_evidence.note: Here *314 is a word-specific variant of PU₂, as in DU-PU₂-RE (PK Za 15, HT Zb 160): dubur ʾIda 'the sanctuary of Ida' (di Mino, Ya Diktu; Davis 2013, 44 n. 46; Facchetti 1999, 132). The word gives no evidence for ḤA.

key_evidence.meaning: damaged ending; Luwian piḫa- comparison unproved
key_evidence.note: Broken before PI; PI overlies an erasure and *314 may be PU₃. Excluded as evidence for *314 = ḤA.

additional_evidence.logogram_317: *317 = LIQḤU 'receipt(s), offering(s)' (√l-q-ḥ). The phonetic complements JU+*317+QE spell lu-…-qe and leave /ḥ/ unwritten.

lipinski_guttural_system.ps_gutturals: PS has 6 'guttural' phonemes: glottal stop ʾ, voiceless laryngal h, voiceless pharyngal ḥ, voiced pharyngal ʿ, voiceless velar fricative ḫ, voiced velar fricative ġ (§19.2).
lipinski_guttural_system.pharyngal_vowel_coloring: In Palaeosyrian: ḥ and ʿ cause a > e in contiguous vowels; ʾ and h do not. This distinguishes pharyngals from laryngals phonologically (§19.5-6). E-vowel signs near guttural positions in Linear A may reflect this.
lipinski_guttural_system.velar_fricative_survival: Canaanite ḫ/ġ survived as distinct from ḥ/ʿ until the Hellenistic period. Greek Γάζα for ġzt, Ἄκη for ʿky prove the distinction was live in 2nd millennium West Semitic (§19.12). The Minoan substrate almost certainly had all 6 gutturals.
lipinski_guttural_system.akkadian_loss: Akkadian reduced all laryngals/pharyngals to ʾ (optional). But Old Assyrian still marked ḥ with dedicated signs—ḥapārum 'to dig' (§19.9). *314=ḤA preserves pharyngal marking in exactly this way.
lipinski_guttural_system.neutralization_chart: Cross-linguistic: Akkadian loses all to ʾ; Geez loses ġ > ʿ; Canaanite/Aramaic ḫ > ḥ and ġ > ʿ (late) (§19.22). Linear A's *314 neutralizing ḥ/ḫ fits the Canaanite pattern.

filled_gaps.other_values: bu, a PU₂ variant, is another possible value: KA-*314-SI kabsi 'young ram' (the lexicon reads kꜣ-ḥs.j, an Egyptian name, with kabsi the rival) and *314-TA-MA buṭma read under it.

filled_gaps.neutralization: Emphatic and marked dentals neutralized into one sign. Distinct from standard DA/TA which neutralize voicing only.

key_evidence.note: Broken before QA. Only this word would take d.

complementary_distribution.qa_cluster: QA-*118 stands in five words (I-QA-*118 twice, QA-*118, QA-*118-SA, QA-*118-RA-RE); QA-DA occurs only inside QA-QA-DA (PE2).
complementary_distribution.same_word_test: DA-SI-*118 uses both standard DA and *118 in one word: the scribe writes the two apart
complementary_distribution.alternatives_eliminated: QA-KI and QA-TI open words with standard signs, and QA-RU stands in QA-QA-RU; the scribes used *118 for a phoneme those signs do not write.

lipinski_emphatic_phonetics.primary_articulation: Emphatics (ṭ, ṣ, q) are pharyngalized/velarized, not glottalized. Pharyngalization is primary—shown by Ugaritic ṭm' > ġm' 'to be thirsty', nṯr > nġr 'to guard' (velar ġ swaps for emphatic, proving shared articulatory base) (§10.9).
lipinski_emphatic_phonetics.vowel_coloring: Emphatic velarization spreads across the entire word (Arabic tafḫīm): a > u near emphatics. East Semitic qurbum for qarbum 'near', inaṣṣur for inaṣṣar 'he guards' (§10.9). This may explain Linear A vowel variation in readings near emphatic consonants.
lipinski_emphatic_phonetics.glottalization_secondary: Ejective (glottalized) emphatics in Ethiopic/Modern South Arabian are secondary—reflect loss of pharyngal ʿ. Linear A substrate (2nd millennium West Semitic) had pharyngalized emphatics (§10.10).
lipinski_emphatic_phonetics.linear_a_implication: *118=ṬA covers pharyngalized ṭ/ḍ. The a>u vowel coloring near emphatics may explain some apparent vowel alternations in corpus readings (e.g., if a word shows -u- where -a- is expected, check for adjacent emphatics).

filled_gaps.other_values: d is possible only in QA-*118-SA; ṯ in two crop words (quṯṯāʾ 'cucumber', ḥaṯ 'unleavened bread').
filled_gaps.logogram: Standing alone after a commodity sign and before a numeral, *118 is the talent, as Linear B *118 L (Bartoněk 2003, 126; Killen 2024, 141; HT24b, Del Freo 2020, 56): resolved.

filled_gaps.evidence: √b-q-r 'cattle' (PA₃-KA-RA-TI = baqarāti), √ʿ-b-d 'servant' (A-PA₃-DI = ʿabadī), √b-n-y 'build' (PA₃-NI-NA = banīna), and the divine name KU-PA₃-PA₃ = Kubaba (HT88), beside KU-PA₃-NU Kubānu and KU-PA₃-NA-TU Kubānatu.
filled_gaps.notes: Standard grid neutralizes P/B voicing. PA₃ breaks the neutralization for /ba/. Revises Gordon 1966 who treated PA₃ as PA allograph.

filled_gaps.evidence: KI-*310-RE = kinnār "lyre" (Hebrew kinnōr). QA-*310-I = qaynī "smith or cultic administrator" (√q-y-n; Arabic qayn, Sabaic qyn). PI-*310-A = pīnā "face, front, portion" (√p-n-y, cf. I-PI-NA-MA). Structural parallel to AU=/aw/: both are VC signs closing syllables.
filled_gaps.notes: Not a phonemic gap in the traditional sense (no missing consonant), but a structural gap: the CV grid cannot represent syllable-closing consonants. VC signs (AU=/aw/, *310=/in/) extend the grid for Semitic CVC morphology. The script adaptation strategy uses both dead vowels (standard approach) and dedicated VC signs (innovation approach) for closed syllables.

filled_gaps.neutralization: Voiced pharyngeal fricative (ayin). No neutralization—dedicated sign for this phoneme.

lipinski_pharyngal_note.vowel_coloring: ʿ (voiced pharyngal) causes a > e shift in contiguous vowels in Palaeosyrian—En-na-i-lī /Ḥenna-'Ilī/, Eb-du-Rašap /'Ebdu-Rašap/ (§19.5-6). This distinguishes ʿ phonologically from ʾ/h which do not trigger the shift.
lipinski_pharyngal_note.cross_linguistic: ʿ preserved in Canaanite, Arabic, ESA; lost in Akkadian (> ʾ > zero) and late Aramaic (> zero). Distinct from ġ (voiced velar fricative) which also causes a > e. Greek Ἄκη for ʿky shows ʿ was NOT transcribed (§19.12).

filled_gaps.neutralization: An optional H-sign covering h, ḥ and ḫ, as cuneiform's Ḫ-series writes West Semitic ḥ and ḫ alike. H is ordinarily unwritten, as in Linear B, where a₂ (ha) is optional (pa-we-a 88 times, pa-we-a₂ 9). Standing alone with a numeral, *21F is the logogram OVISf, ewe (HT 132, ZA 9, ZA 26a).

lipinski_laryngal_note.h_vs_pharyngals: h (voiceless laryngal) does NOT cause a > e vowel coloring, unlike ḥ and ʿ (§19.5-6).
lipinski_laryngal_note.loss_pattern: h is the most fragile guttural—lost earliest and most widely. Akkadian lost it (> ʾ > zero) by Old Babylonian. Canaanite preserved it in spelling but weakened in pronunciation. Linear A writes it optionally, with *21F.
lipinski_laryngal_note.three_guttural_signs: Lipiński's three-way distinction (laryngal h without vowel colouring, pharyngal ḥ and ʿ with a > e) is not a three-sign system in Linear A: *306 writes ʿ, *314 ḥ or ḫ, and *21F optionally h, ḥ or ḫ. ʾ is written with the vowel signs; ġ falls in the K-class or with ʿ.

open_gaps.description: Voiced pharyngeal fricative (Hebrew/Arabic ayin). One of the most frequent consonants in Semitic—appears in ʿabd 'servant', ʿam 'people', ʿayin 'eye/spring', ʿaštar 'Ishtar'. Egyptian ꜥ is cognate.

languages_requiring.northwest_semitic: Very frequent—roots with ʿ are core vocabulary
languages_requiring.middle_egyptian: ꜥ in names and titles (e.g., Rꜥ 'Ra')

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: May be written as a vowel sign (ʿa → A, ʿi → I) or omitted entirely. Gordon proposed ʿa > o shift in some Semitic substrates. A dedicated sign would be expected only if ʿ-initial words are frequent enough to cause ambiguity.

open_gaps.description: Glottal stop (Hebrew/Arabic aleph). Extremely frequent—initial position in ʾab 'father', ʾel 'god', ʾadon 'lord'. Egyptian ꜣ (aleph) in kꜣ, names.

languages_requiring.northwest_semitic: Very frequent—initial aleph in most divine names and basic vocabulary

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: Almost certainly written as the pure vowel signs (A, E, I, O, U) in initial position. Internal glottal stop may be omitted or represented by vowel hiatus. A dedicated sign is unlikely—vowel signs already serve this function in most syllabaries.

candidate_signs.rationale: Standard practice in CV syllabaries: glottal stop is implicit in word-initial vowel signs.

open_gaps.note: Bare vowel signs (A, E, I, O, U) serve as ʾa, ʾe, ʾi, ʾo, ʾu in word-initial position (standard CV syllabary practice). *324 = ʾA is an alternate only: its primary is SO (speculative, 0.30), since Linear A has no other SO sign and plain A already writes /ʔa/.

open_gaps.description: Voiceless laryngeal fricative (Hebrew he). Distinct from pharyngeal ḥ. Frequent in Semitic pronouns (hu, hi), demonstratives, and roots.

languages_requiring.luwian: ḫ overlaps but distinct from plain h
languages_requiring.middle_egyptian: h distinct from ḥ/ḫ in Egyptian phonology

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: No HA/HE/HI/HO/HU series exists in the standard grid. Could be: (1) merged with *314 ḤA-class, (2) omitted, (3) written as a vowel, or (4) represented by an unidentified unknown sign.
open_gaps.filled_by: *21F = HA, an optional H-sign (h, ḥ, ḫ), proposed

open_gaps.description: Emphatic sibilant (Hebrew tsade). Distinct from s/š/z but neutralized into S-class in standard grid. Appears in √ṣ-d-q 'righteous', √ṣ-l-m 'image', √ṣ-r-r 'bind'.

languages_requiring.northwest_semitic: Moderate frequency—important roots but less common than s/š

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: Probably neutralized into the S-class (SA/SE/SI/SO/SU) without a dedicated sign. A separate sign would only be expected if S-class neutralization creates systematic ambiguity.

candidate_signs.rationale: Read as QI (K-class), so *34 fills the /qi/ slot, not the emphatic sibilant gap; ṢA and ṢI each misread two of its words. The gap stays LIKELY_NEUTRALIZED into the S-class.
Z-class might differentiate some emphatic sibilant contexts from S-class

lipinski_phonetics.emphatic_realization: ṣ realized as affricate [ts]—not just modern; attested in Demotic tspn for ṣpn 'north' and possibly Greek αστηρ for ḥsr (§14.7). Amharic and Gafat preserve [ts] pronunciation.
lipinski_phonetics.lateral_merger: PS voiceless lateral ś merged with š in most languages by 2nd millennium (§16.1). Greek βάλσαμον from bśm 'balsam' preserves the lateral character (λσ transcribing ś). SA-series signs absorb both ś and š.
lipinski_phonetics.sibilant_burden: The SA/SI/SU series neutralizes PS s, š, ś, ṣ, and possibly ṯ (after Canaanite merger)—up to 5 original phonemes in one sign series. This matches cuneiform practice where SA/ŠA partially overlapped (§13.5).

open_gaps.description: Voiceless and voiced interdentals. Proto-Semitic *ṯ and *ḏ survive in Ugaritic and early Canaanite but merge with sibilants or dentals in later languages. If Minoan Semitic preserves archaic features, these might be distinguished.
open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: Almost certainly merged into S-class (ṯ > š/s) and D/T-class (ḏ > d/z). Separate signs unlikely unless the Minoan Semitic substrate is very archaic.

candidate_signs.assigned_value: ṮU (/θu/), with ZU (/zu/) a second value; proposed
candidate_signs.rationale: ZU writes two values, as SA writes s and š. ṯu is primary: A-ZU-RA = ʾAṯrat or ʾAṯirat (KNZc7), MA-ZU = maṯu beside Linear B ma-*79, and no scribe alternates ZU with another sign. zu is the second value, on RU-ZU-NA = rāzin (PS *z).

*305-RU = ḏarʿ- 'seed, grain' (√ḏ-r-ʿ, distance 0.100) on the HT10a emmer allocation, the one ḏ-root cell. ḏ is taken from the logogram reading ḎABBĀḤŪ (√ḏ-b-ḥ). DA co-occurs on 5 tablets. With ZU = /ṯu/ it gives the interdental pair. ṯa is another possible value (KA-*305, read ka-ḏā 'thus', rival kaṯ 'flask').
PK1 writes TA and TA₂ both. KI-RE-TA₂ = krt 'Kret' (distance 0.000).
candidate_signs.alternate_rationale: Would complete ZU=/ṯu/ pair and explain PK1 contrast, but √k-r-ṯ is not a real PS root—no anchor word.

open_gaps.note: ZU = /ṯu/ (0.74) and *305 = /ḏa/ (0.65) are proposed; TA₂ is /ta/ (Linear B *66), with /ṯa/ an alternate at 0.32.

lipinski_chronology.ps_system: PS has three interdentals: ṯ [θ], ḏ [ð], emphatic ẓ. These are distinct phonemes, not allophones.

merger_patterns.canaanite: ṯ > š, ḏ > z, ẓ > ṣ—merger complete by 13th c. BCE (22-letter alphabet)
merger_patterns.aramaic: ṯ > t, ḏ > d, ẓ > ṭ—different target (dentals, not sibilants)
merger_patterns.akkadian: ṯ > š (ŠA series), ḏ > z (ZA series)—early merger
merger_patterns.amorite: ṯ/š distinction preserved in 2nd millennium cuneiform names (§13.4)

lipinski_chronology.linear_a_implication: Linear A texts (17th–15th c. BCE) predate the Canaanite merger. A NWS substrate of this period should preserve interdentals, as ZU = ṯu and *305 = ḏa propose. Amorite—the closest 2nd-millennium NWS comparandum—also preserves the distinction.

open_gaps.description: Voiced velar stop. Neutralized under K-class (which covers k/g/q). A separate G-series would exist only if the K-class neutralization fails systematically.

languages_requiring.northwest_semitic: Moderate—g-roots exist but K-class handles them
languages_requiring.luwian: k/g distinction relevant in Anatolian names

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: K-class neutralization. No dedicated G-series expected.
open_gaps.notes: With *34 read as QI, the readings qi, gi and ga give the same root matches, so nothing separates a G-series from the K-class.

lipinski_velar_system.ps_inventory: PS has three velars: voiceless k, voiced g, emphatic q. Arabic q is 'fortis' (Sibawayh's maġhūra), not necessarily voiced (§18.2).
lipinski_velar_system.cuneiform_neutralization: Cuneiform never distinguishes final k/g/q. Initial distinction partial and late (Old Babylonian on). AG = ag/ak/aq, GAB = gab/qab, GIM = gim/kim/qim (§18.3). Linear A's KA/KI/KU neutralization is the exact parallel.
lipinski_velar_system.neo_assyrian: In Neo-Assyrian, [g] and [k] are positional variants—voiced intervocalically. Aramaic mngsr for Mannu-kišarri shows the scribal confusion (§18.4).
lipinski_velar_system.velar_fricatives: PS also has voiceless ḫ and voiced ġ (velar fricatives, distinct from plosives k/g). Canaanite ḫ/ġ survived as distinct from ḥ/ʿ until the Hellenistic period—Greek Γάζα for ġzt proves ġ in 2nd-millennium Canaanite (§19.12). These are separate from the k/g/q plosive set.
lipinski_velar_system.linear_a_implication: Three-way k/g/q neutralization under KA-series is typologically normal for syllabic scripts encoding Semitic. The partial QA/QE/QI extension for emphatic uvular mirrors cuneiform attempts at the same distinction.

open_gaps.description: Voiced velar fricative (Arabic ġayn). Distinct from voiced velar plosive /g/ and from voiced pharyngal /ʿ/. Lipiński §19.12 proves ġ survived as a distinct phoneme in 2nd-millennium Canaanite—Greek Γάζα for ġzt, Γοφερα for Hebrew ʿOprā show scribes heard it as /g/ not /ʿ/. PS roots with ġ: √ṣ-ġ-r 'to be small', √n-ġ-r 'to guard' (Ugaritic nġr < nṯr).

languages_requiring.northwest_semitic: Distinct from ʿ until Hellenistic period. Roots with ġ exist but are low-frequency.

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: Probably neutralized into K-series (KA/KI/KU), since Greek scribes transcribed ġ as Γ (a velar plosive). Alternatively merged with *306 (ʿA) as the ġ > ʿ merger was already underway in Canaanite.
open_gaps.notes: Lipiński §19.12 establishes that ġ was phonemically distinct from ʿ in 2nd-millennium Canaanite—Linear A's substrate almost certainly had it. The neutralization target is ambiguous: K-class (phonetic similarity to /g/) or *306 ʿA-class (later Canaanite merger ġ > ʿ). No corpus evidence distinguishes the two strategies.

lipinski_reference.key_evidence: Greek Γάζα (ġzt), Γοφερα (ġufrā) vs Ἄκη (ʿky)—Greek scribes distinguished ġ (Γ) from ʿ (zero/vowel). Palaeosyrian: ġ causes a > e like ḥ/ʿ do, distinguishing it from ḫ (§19.5-6). Ugaritic preserves ġ as a separate letter.
lipinski_reference.merger_timeline: Canaanite ġ > ʿ merger late (post-Hellenistic in Hebrew). In the 17th–15th c. BCE window of Linear A, ġ was almost certainly a live phoneme.

open_gaps.description: Even where the consonant gap is filled (e.g., *314 = ḤA, *118 = ṬA), only the /a/ vowel combination is identified. Other vowel combinations for these consonants may exist as separate signs, or the /a/ sign may serve polyvalently for all vowels.

languages_requiring.northwest_semitic: Any consonant can combine with any vowel

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: Polyvalent use of /a/-column signs. None of ~130 extended signs is a strong candidate for a dedicated non-/a/ guttural sign. Each extra consonant has one sign covering all vowel contexts: *314=Ḥ(V), *118=Ṭ(V), *306=ʿ(V), *21F=H(V). Parallels cuneiform practice where guttural signs are vocalically ambiguous.

candidate_signs.rationale: *305 = syllabogram /ḏa/ and logogram ḎABBĀḤŪ, both proposed.
*86 = /na/, speculative (0.40): 16 of its 24 tokens stand alone, and NA and *301 already write na.

open_gaps.description: With AU = /aw/ (resolved) and *310 = /in/ (proposed) as VC signs, the script may contain additional VC signs for other common syllable-closing patterns. Semitic morphology requires coda consonants in most words. Some unknown signs with medial distribution may be VC rather than CV.

languages_requiring.northwest_semitic: CVC syllables are fundamental to Semitic morphology

open_gaps.likely_script_strategy: Most closed syllables handled by dead vowels (standard CV approach). VC signs are innovations for the most frequent coda patterns. /aw/ and /in/ are the two VC signs on record.

open_gaps.description: /bu/ CV slot (PA₃ = /ba/, PU = /pu/): the voiced labial of the u-row.
open_gaps.candidate_note: *325 = BU (0.40): U-*325-ZA / A-*325-ZA = ʾubūs / ʾabūs 'stall, storehouse' (Akk. abūsu, pl. ubsātu); rival /ḫu/, ʾuḫuzza(t) 'holding'. The VC /at/ is an alternate (0.25).

open_gaps.description: /bi/ CV slot: PA/PA₃ prove the script splits p/b in the a-row; no i-row sign carries the voiced labial. Sister gap of voiced_labial_bu.
open_gaps.candidate_note: *333 = BI (speculative): renders bīdi Našūka / bīdi Sūka (Ugaritic bd custody formula) on the HTWc3009/3010 roundel pair and biśāmu 'balsam' (√b-ś-m, pre-Canaanite-shift bōśem) on MOZf1. PI-DI unattested corpus-wide (no collision).

syllabic_behavior_index.description: Positional behaviour of frequent unknown signs, counted in corpus.json: a word token is split at '-' into sign positions and at '+' into the signs of a ligature; a token of one position stands alone. Signs found across word positions are likely syllabic; signs mostly standing alone are likely logographic.

signs.assessment: SYLLABIC and logographic: NA (proposed) and the NWY logogram; A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA, read A-TA-I-NA-WA-JA, = ʾatainawaya 'I make myself a dwelling' (√n-w-y; di Mino, Ya Diktu)
SYLLABIC—ṬA (proposed); standing alone before a numeral, the talent logogram (resolved)
SYLLABIC and logographic: an optional H-sign (h, ḥ, ḫ), proposed; standing alone with a numeral, the logogram OVISf
dual function: logogram ḎABBĀḤŪ and syllabogram /ḏa/, both proposed

candidate_logogram.evidence: PK Za 8 JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE = PK Za 15 JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE: *307 writes DU, 'O Dikte, Mistress of the Dubur' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). VIR+*307 'sanctuary personnel' (KH 9, KH 14); TI-NI-TA · *307 'Tinit of the Sanctuary' (HT 27a); *307 doubled (A 638) heads HT 36, 85a and 97a. PE Wy 5 OLE *307 is two signs.

signs.assessment: VC SYLLABLE—IN (/in/), proposed. Structural parallel to AU=/aw/: it closes syllables. Anchor: KI-*310-RE = kinnār (Hebrew kinnōr "lyre").
